title: OwlCrate Alternatives: 6 Book Boxes Like OwlCrate - Cratejoy
summary: Looking for an OwlCrate alternative? Compare six book boxes by price, format, and age, from YA fantasy special editions to signed romance and middle grade.
body_markdown:
## The alternatives


More YA books a month


### Owl Post Books YA Imagination Box vs OwlCrate


1st box


50% off


Preferred Seller


[14 & Up Young Adult Imagination Box and Mini Subscriptions](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/bowl-post-books-ya-fantasy-imagination-subscription-bowlpostbooks) by Owl Post Books


From $19.99 / box


Free shipping


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/bowl-post-books-ya-fantasy-imagination-subscription-bowlpostbooks)


**Best for:** The 14-and-up bookworm who finishes one book by the 5th and wants the next two on the shelf.


Owl Post Books trades the special edition for volume. The Box sends three brand-new YA hardcovers a month in an interactive box, and the Mini sends one in a colorful mailer. A short quiz steers the picks, with options such as fantasy, romance, dystopian, mystery, first in a series, or stand-alone, and every book is the reader’s to keep.


#### What feels familiar


New YA hardcovers, chosen by someone else, on a monthly rhythm. Fantasy is one of the quiz answers, so the genre can stay the same.


#### What changes


No signed copies, no exclusive covers, and no themed pins or mugs. Three books cost $40 with shipping included, about what one OwlCrate box costs before its shipping is added. Boxes go by USPS Media Mail, which takes three to seven days.


Fantasy for less


### SplureBox Fantasy Books Club vs OwlCrate


1st box


50% off


Preferred Seller


[Fantasy Books Club](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/fantasy-books-club-splurebox) by SplureBox


From $15.99 / box


Free shipping


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/fantasy-books-club-splurebox)


**Best for:** Fantasy fans who want a new hardcover each month and don’t collect editions.


SplureBox runs one-genre clubs, and its fantasy club sends handpicked hardcover fantasy along with bookish products, mixing bestselling authors with names you haven’t met yet. At $18.99 a month with free shipping, it costs less than half of an OwlCrate box once US shipping is added.


#### What feels familiar


Fantasy only, in hardcover, with someone else doing the choosing and a bookish extra in the box.


#### What changes


The books are regular editions, not signed or redesigned, and the club covers fantasy in general rather than YA. The listing doesn’t say how many books arrive each month. SplureBox ships from Czechia, so expect a longer trip than a domestic box.


A signed book every month


### Reveal Book Box vs OwlCrate


[*Individual Signed Romance Book (No frills)*](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/reveal-book-box) by Reveal Book Box


From $13.95 / box


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/reveal-book-box)


**Best for:** The OwlCrate Romance or Romantasy waitlister who mostly wanted the signature.


Reveal Book Box sends one romance novel a month, signed by its author, matched to the subgenres and tropes you pick at checkout. The list runs from enemies to lovers and small town to rom-com, and it includes YA romance. This is the seller’s no-frills option: the book and nothing packed around it.


#### What feels familiar


A signed copy in every box. At $13.95 a month, one book costs less than half of OwlCrate’s $31.99 quarterly Romance box, and there’s no waitlist.


#### What changes


Romance only, and no fantasy guarantee. There are no goodies and no special-edition design. It ships by USPS within 10 business days, and only to US addresses.


After OwlCrate Jr.


### beTWEEN the Bookends vs OwlCrate


15% off


Preferred Seller


[beTWEEN the Bookends: Tween Book and Lifestyle Box](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/bbetween-the-bookends-bbetweenthebookends) by beTWEEN the Bookends


From $20.00 / box


Ships fast


Free shipping


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/bbetween-the-bookends-bbetweenthebookends)


**Best for:** A middle-grade bookworm, 8 and up, who loved OwlCrate Jr. or has watched an older sibling open OwlCrate boxes.


OwlCrate Jr. was OwlCrate’s box for middle-grade kids, and beTWEEN the Bookends fills that spot with a themed box of its own. The full box holds two or three middle-grade novels and six to eight items, from stationery and bookish goodies to bath products, jewelry, and sweets. It’s put together by Jillian, a teen who reads every book and tests every product before it ships.


#### What feels familiar


A themed monthly box where the book comes with things to use while reading it, pitched at an age OwlCrate’s YA boxes skip.


#### What changes


Books come as a mix of hardcover and paperback, and none are signed editions. The full box leans toward tween girls. The gender-neutral version drops the beauty and jewelry items, and a books-only version sends the novels with a bookmark.


Closest to OwlCrate


### FairyLoot vs OwlCrate


[FairyLoot’s YA Book + Items subscription](https://fairyloot.com/subscription-plan/ya-book-items-subscription/) is the one to try if you want the same thing from a different curator.


**Best for:** Collectors who want a second shelf of exclusive YA fantasy editions.


FairyLoot’s flagship box sends an exclusive edition of a newly released YA fantasy hardcover with four or five items built around the monthly theme. It also runs book-only YA, adult fantasy, and romantasy plans, plus quarterly epic and cozy fantasy boxes. US and Canadian subscribers order from a separate store that prices in dollars.


#### What feels familiar


Nearly everything: the format, the genre, the exclusive editions, and the themed extras.


#### What changes


A different set of books and designers, and shipping and tax come on top of the monthly price. FairyLoot’s plans can fill up, so you may join a waitlist first. It isn’t sold on Cratejoy.


You pick the special edition


### LitJoy To Bee Read vs OwlCrate


[LitJoy’s To Bee Read subscription](https://litjoycrate.com/pages/to-bee-read-book-box-subscription) hands you the choice of book.


**Best for:** A collector who’d rather choose the book than be surprised by it.


Each quarter LitJoy shows two books, and during customization week you choose one. It arrives as a signed LitJoy Edition. The book-only plan stops there, while the Standard box adds five items (you choose three and two are a surprise) and the Deluxe adds eight. LitJoy works across YA and adult titles in fantasy, romance, dystopian, mystery, and more.


#### What feels familiar


Signed special editions and themed bookish extras, from a company that designs its own editions.


#### What changes


Four boxes a year instead of twelve, and the choosing happens in a set window each quarter. Miss it on a Standard or Deluxe box and LitJoy picks your items. It isn’t YA-fantasy only, and it isn’t sold on Cratejoy.
